ai.title: Wrap fetch to retry transient network errors
ai.summary: Global fetch wrapped in `fetchWithRetryableNetworkErrors` to rethrow transient connection failures (socket closed/reset, connection refused) as retryable `APICallError`s. This fixes Bun's plain Error throws being ignored by AI SDK's auto-retry logic, enabling exponential backoff for brief network blips. Scope includes `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, `common/src/util/error.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts`, and `sdk/src/run.ts`. `isTransientNetworkError` detects specific message substrings and error codes to distinguish dropped connections from server errors.

eli5.text: If your internet connection hiccups for just a moment during a conversation with the assistant (like a dropped call that reconnects), the request now automatically retries instead of failing completely. This applies to anyone running agent steps or using the SDK's run function, which now recognize these specific 'socket closed' or 'connection refused' errors and treat them as temporary, triggering the built-in retry logic that was previously ignoring them. You would notice fewer failures and shorter interruption messages guiding you to check your network, as the system now handles these brief connection blips silently in the background.

The most noticeable ones make chat history reliable even if the program crashes or closes unexpectedly, so your saved conversations are less likely to get cut off or corrupted. The message list also handles being interrupted when a free session ends, holding unsent messages and trying them again later instead of dropping them. A few behind-the-scenes pieces, like retrying when the network hiccups and small changes to how the program starts up, are in place but won't change what you see on screen.

The feature is live today behind the scenes, but only external test suites or advanced integrations that supply these callbacks would observe any difference.

ai.title: SDK file tools honor absolute cwd and escape project boundaries

facts: Anthropic requires a top-level `type: 'object'`. Object schemas already carry it; union/intersection schemas (anyOf/allOf) don't, backfill it.

Convert tool definitions to Anthropic format for accurate token counting Tool definitions are stored as { [name]: { description, inputSchema } } Anthropic count_tokens API expects [{ name, description, input_schema }] Convert tool definitions to Anthropic format for accurate token counting.

Tool definitions are stored as { [name]: { description, inputSchema } }, where inputSchema is a Zod schema. Anthropic's count_tokens API expects [{ name, description, input_schema }] with input_schema being real JSON Schema (with a top-level `type: 'object'`), see toTokenCountInputSchema.

ai.title: Convert Zod tool schemas to JSON Schema for Anthropic token counting
ai.summary: Added `toTokenCountInputSchema` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` to convert Zod `inputSchema` to JSON Schema before sending to Anthropic's `count_tokens` API. Raw Zod serialization previously shipped internals like `def`/`shape`, causing inaccurate token counts and `tools.N.custom.input_schema.type: Field required` errors for union/intersection schemas lacking a top-level `type`. The fix uses `z.toJSONSchema` with `io: 'input'`, strips `$schema`, and backfills `type: 'object'` if missing.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks the token-counting service how many words are in your tools, it now sends the tool definitions with a clean JSON-Schema description, avoiding a previous format that included technical clutter that inflated the count and made a few tool types fail entirely. This makes the token counts that the system uses to manage the length of your conversation noticeably more accurate and keeps the agent runtime from breaking mid-task when those tools are involved.

facts: Treat missing / null / empty-string as absent (valid JSON Schema `type` is always a non-empty string or array).

ai.title: Harden type backfill in run-agent-step.ts
ai.summary: The type backfill logic in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` now treats missing, null, and empty-string `type` values as absent. This ensures Anthropic's `type: 'object'` requirement is met for union/intersection schemas lacking a valid type. Scope is limited to the agent runtime schema conversion.

eli5.text: If you use the agent runtime, the assistant can now correctly send certain input schemas to Anthropic models that previously failed because a required field was missing, null, or empty. The system now treats those invalid values as if they were absent and automatically adds the required field, preventing API errors during schema conversion. This fix is live today and applies whenever the runtime converts input schemas for Anthropic-compatible models.
